Prior and posterior distributions of a fit's parameters

Source: R/ctStanPlotPost.R
ctPlotPosterior.Rd

Plots, for each free population parameter of a fit, its prior and its posterior on the natural scale. This covers the population mean, and for an individually varying parameter the population standard deviation at each level it varies at. Works for fits from either backend. The prior is ctsem's normal(0,1) raw prior passed through each parameter's transform, which is the prior used with priors = TRUE. For a fit made without priors, the plot shows how far the data moved each parameter from where that prior would put it. The posterior comes from the fit's draws, which are posterior draws for a sampled fit, and approximate ones from ctFitUncertainty for an optimized fit. ctStanPlotPost is an alias.

Usage

ctPlotPosterior(
  obj,
  rows = "all",
  npp = 4,
  priorwidth = TRUE,
  smoothness = 1,
  priorsamples = 10000,
  plot = TRUE,
  wait = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

obj

A fit from ctFit, on either backend. A model on its own has no posterior; plot(model) plots its priors.

rows

Character string 'all', or which parameters to plot, by position in the fit's free population parameters, in parameter order.

npp

Integer number of parameters to show per page.

priorwidth

if TRUE, plots will be scaled to show bulk of both the prior and posterior distributions. If FALSE, scale is based only on the posterior.

smoothness

Positive numeric – multiplier to modify smoothness of density plots, higher is smoother but can cause plots to exceed natural boundaries, such as standard deviations below zero.

priorsamples

number of samples from prior to use. More is slower.

plot

Logical, if FALSE, ggplot objects are returned in a list instead of plotting.

wait

If true, user is prompted to continue before plotting next graph. If false, graphs are plotted one after another without waiting.

...

For a stan fit, passed to the preparation of the prior draws: cores = x will speed things up, where x is the number of cpu cores to use. A julia fit takes nothing here.

Value

With plot = TRUE, NULL invisibly, having drawn the plots; with plot = FALSE, a list of ggplot objects.

Examples

# \donttest{
# The prior (blue) and posterior (red) of the third and fourth population
# parameters, the auto effect of eta1 and the effect of eta2 on eta1. A
# posterior much narrower than its prior shows that the data determine the
# parameter.
ctPlotPosterior(ctstantestfit, rows = 3:4)
# }
